title: 13-17s recall latency = daemon ping (≤1.5s) + dead local uv spawn (~2s) + DB uv spawn (≤12s), all SEQUENTIAL despite the header claiming parallel; each prompt pays TWO uv-run cold starts

evidence.quote: * 3. Run local-memory + DB-memory checks in parallel

const local = checkLocalMemory(recallQuery, projectDir);
  const [db, dbTimedOut] = checkDbMemory(recallQuery, projectDir, daemonReady);
timeout: useHybrid ? 12000 : 5000,

observe_how: spawnSync is blocking; the two child-process recalls run back-to-back after the isDaemonReady TCP ping (1500ms budget, embedding-client.ts DEFAULT_PING_TIMEOUT_MS). Worst case: 1.5 + 2.0 + 12.0 = 15.5s, matching SEED-08's observed 13-17s. The uv startup tax (~2.2s per the in-file comment) is paid twice per prompt. New root-cause evidence for SEED-08: the dominant terms are the duplicated uv spawn plus serialization, not the Python query itself (text-only measured ~750ms warm per line 233 comment).
telemetry: memory-recall.jsonl total_elapsed_ms field per row; SUMMARY.md cites 13-17s warm hybrid.

title: LOCAL_SCORE_NORMALIZE (0.1) was calibrated against text-only ts_rank, not hybrid RRF — once D3c-02 is fixed, local rows (~0.05) will systematically outrank RRF DB rows (0.01-0.03) in the merge and can shadow all 3 top slots, re-creating the exact local-shadowing Wave 3 removed

evidence.quote:
* Local index returns cosine-ish similarity (~0.5 typical) while the DB path
 * returns ts_rank (0.0001–0.1) plus a 0.1 ILIKE fallback. Multiplying local
 * scores by this factor brings them into the ts_rank range so the merge sort

const TEXT_ONLY_FLOOR = 0.05;  // FTS ts_rank scores: 0.05-0.5 typical
const HYBRID_FLOOR = 0.01;     // RRF fused scores: 0.01-0.03 typical
const LOCAL_SCORE_NORMALIZE = 0.1;

causal_links: latent today ONLY because of D3c-02 (local never returns); fixing D3c-02 without recalibrating activates this
ironic regression vector: Wave 3's stated purpose was to de-shadow local memory (file header L21-22) — the un-recalibrated normalizer re-shadows in the opposite direction in hybrid mode
observe_how: Arithmetic from the file's own constants: local similarity ~0.5 x 0.1 = ~0.05; hybrid RRF DB scores are 0.01-0.03 per the HYBRID_FLOOR comment. mergeResults sorts descending and slices to top 3, and checkLocalMemory returns up to 3 rows — so 3 local rows at ~0.05 evict every DB hybrid row regardless of relevance. Needs a mode-aware normalizer (or rank-based merge) when daemonReady.
telemetry: After fixing D3c-02, watch memory-recall.jsonl source field: a sudden flip to predominantly 'local'/'merged' in hybrid mode with stable top_score ~0.05 is this bug expressing.

title: proposed_bus_updates has NO consumer: the 'downstream SubagentStop writer' asserted in present tense by both the code and the boundary rule does not exist anywhere in hooks/src - every proposal (and the persistable/corpus_signature machinery feeding it) is computed and dropped

evidence.quote:

A downstream `SubagentStop` writer revalidates before applying; stale proposals are dropped. The facade never mutates `context.json`.

telemetry: Repo-wide grep for proposed_bus_updates matches only code-intel.mjs, code-intel.test.sh, the boundary rule, and harvest snapshots - zero matches in .claude/hooks/src/. The 14 hooks-src files mentioning SubagentStop are pattern-framework files, none a bus-proposal applier.

title: Codex finding #5 fix does not enforce its own documented invariant: persistable accepts a bare `name` (code: uri || rawQualified || name) while the comment requires 'a real filePath/uri OR a real qualifiedName' - two same-named, filePath-less nodes still collide on signature_hash AND pass the bus-proposal filter

evidence.quote: const persistable = !!(uri || rawQualified || name);

observe_how: node -e import: toScipId({name:'render'}) and a second {name:'render'} (no filePath, no qualifiedName) return persistable:true with IDENTICAL signature_hash (hash input is ''|unknown|render|unknown|0 for both) - exactly the merged-bus-update collision the fix claims to prevent. The shipped test only covers name:'' (empty), so the gap is invisible to the suite. Practical exposure is currently latent (no proposal consumer, D4b-03) and low (codegraph nodes normally carry filePath), but the fix-vs-spec mismatch is real: drop `|| name` or add name to the documented invariant.

title: Facade codegraph telemetry is unjoinable: bus_id is 'unknown' on 35/37 live codegraph rows (who-calls/find-symbol never read the bus), the schema's `agent` field is never set, and correlation_id is a fresh randomUUID emitted on exactly one row - C.3's telemetry watch cannot attribute codegraph usage to any session or agent

evidence.quote:
appendIntelRow({
    bus_id: response.bus_id || 'unknown',
"bus_id":"unknown","specialist":"codegraph","query_type":"who-calls","result_count":13
L3 specialists READ the bus to bias queries and return *proposed* updates to the facade; they never write L2 directly (§13 Q2).

telemetry: grep .claude/logs/intel-bus.jsonl: 37 codegraph rows total, 35 with "bus_id":"unknown" (the 2 non-unknown are code-context fused rows, which do call readBus). Harvest table-intel-bus.json: live by_agent = {null: 318} - no emitter sets agent; corr-null 60.7% is the hook emitters, but the facade's per-call randomUUID is functionally a row id, not a correlation (each call emits exactly one row, so it ties nothing).
observe_how: Only code-context/recall/bus call readBus(); the two hottest codegraph paths (who-calls, find-symbol) skip it entirely - so response.bus_id is undefined and telemetry falls back to 'unknown'. This also means the rule's 'specialists READ the bus to bias queries' is unimplemented for those paths (no focus biasing of codegraph results). Fix: call discoverBus() (cheap) in who-calls/find-symbol for the telemetry stamp, and set agent from env when available.

evidence.quote: const PROJECT_DIR = process.env.CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR || process.cwd();
const path = join(PROJECT_DIR, '.claude', 'logs', 'intel-bus.jsonl');
"$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR" && node "$CLI" find-symbol runCodegraph)"

telemetry: git status at review SHA still shows untracked `?? scripts/.claude/` - the artifact the seed says was quarantined is back (or never left), consistent with the test re-creating it.
observe_how: The C.2 nested-cwd mitigation (#6) fixed QUERY targeting (cwd=repoRoot + -p repoRoot) but not the TELEMETRY and BUS-DISCOVERY anchors, which still use PROJECT_DIR: from a nested cwd the telemetry lands in <cwd>/.claude/logs and bus discovery scans <cwd>/.claude/cache/session (silently finding nothing). repoRoot() already exists and is the correct anchor for both. The mitigation-#6 test at test.sh:83 deterministically reproduces the junk on every test run; it should set CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (or CCV3_BUS_OFF=1) like the telemetry tests do.
